mainTopic: תמר's modesty and her refusal to shame יהודה, יהודה's public admission and its rewards, and אבשלום's pride in his hair and his punishment through it.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a דרשה about אברהם אבינו: he got every guest to thank and bless הקב"ה after eating. The גמרא then works through the story of יהודה and תמר. רבי אלעזר explains that תמר always covered her face in יהודה's house, which is why he did not recognize her on the road. From her modesty we learn that a modest daughter-in-law merits kings and prophets, like דוד and ישעיהו. The גמרא explains the odd words of the story: סמאל and גבריאל moved her proof-items, she became like a mute dove, and the word מכתם is read three ways as praise of דוד. תמר only hinted to יהודה rather than naming him, which teaches that it is better to be thrown into a fiery furnace than to shame someone in public. יהודה's open admission earned him the whole name of ה׳ inside his own name, and also the rescue of חנניה, מישאל and עזריה from the fire. Next the גמרא turns to אבשלום, who sinned through pride in his hair and was hung by his hair. דוד's eight cries of 'my son' raised him out of גיהנם. The amud ends in the middle of a דרשה on the monument אבשלום set up for himself, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: אברהם got others to call out God's name
steps.stepSummary: The word ויקרא is read as ויקריא: אברהם caused every passerby to call out הקב"ה's name.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it as ויקריא, 'he caused others to call.' This teaches that אברהם אבינו caused the name of הקב"ה to be called out by the mouth of every person who passed by.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a דרשה from the previous lines. It reads the word in the פסוק as 'he made others call' instead of 'he called.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing one vowel shifts the meaning. Read the plain way, אברהם himself called in הקב"ה's name. Read as ויקריא, he got other people to do it, so his influence reached every traveler.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This teaches': introduces a lesson learned from a פסוק

phrases.english: Rather, read it 'vayakri': he caused others to call.
phrases.notes: The פסוק (בראשית 21:33) is written ויקרא, 'he called,' but the גמרא reads it as 'he made others call.'

phrases.english: This teaches that Abraham our forefather caused to be called
the name of the Holy One, Blessed be He
in the mouth of every passerby.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a דרשה begun just before this section, rereading ויקרא as ויקריא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אברהם caused all passersby to call out הקב"ה's name.

steps.title: How did he do it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how אברהם got passersby to call out הקב"ה's name.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so?
steps.whatsHappening: This short question sets up the next step. The גמרא wants to know how this actually worked in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The דרשה only told us the result: passersby called out הקב"ה's name. The question asks for the method, and the answer comes right after.

keyTerms.meaning: 'How so?': asks for the practical details

phrases.english: How so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the method behind the דרשה in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical way אברהם led guests to praise הקב"ה.

steps.title: אברהם told his guests to bless God
steps.stepSummary: When guests tried to thank אברהם after the meal, he told them the food was really הקב"ה's and they should bless Him.
steps.simpleTranslation: After they ate and drank, they stood up to bless him. He said to them: Did you eat from what is mine? You ate from what belongs to the God of the world! Thank, praise and bless the One Who spoke and the world came to be.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. אברהם turned his guests' thanks toward הקב"ה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The guests naturally wanted to thank their host. אברהם used that moment to teach them that everything comes from הקב"ה, so they ended up blessing Him. This is how he 'made others call' in הקב"ה's name.

keyTerms.meaning: To bless him (to thank the host)
The One Who spoke and the world came to be

steps.whatToRemember: ויקריא means אברהם got others to praise הקב"ה, by teaching his guests that their food really came from Him.

phrases.english: After they had eaten and drunk,
phrases.notes: 'They' means אברהם's guests.

phrases.english: they stood up to bless him.
He said to them: Did you eat from what is mine?
You ate from what belongs to the God of the world!
Thank, praise and bless
the One Who spoke and the world came to be.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question כיצד from step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He redirected his guests' thanks to הקב"ה, telling them the food was His.

steps.title: Why would a covered face suggest a prostitute?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says יהודה thought תמר was a זונה because she covered her face. The גמרא asks how that makes sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'When יהודה saw her, he thought she was a prostitute, because she had covered her face.' Because she covered her face he thought she was a prostitute?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the story of יהודה and תמר. It challenges the plain reading of a פסוק that seems backward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Covering the face looks like modesty, not like what a זונה would do. So 'because she covered her face' seems like a strange reason for יהודה's mistake. The גמרא needs a different way to read the פסוק.
steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether יהודה made a mistake. It is about the reason the פסוק gives: a covered face seems like the opposite of a sign of a זונה.

phrases.english: 'When Judah saw her, he thought her to be a prostitute,'
phrases.notes: בראשית 38:15

phrases.english: 'for she had covered her face.'
Because she covered her face, he thought she was a prostitute?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the topic of יהודה and תמר after finishing the אברהם דרשה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plain reading of the reason in בראשית 38:15.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A covered face points to modesty, so it cannot explain why יהודה thought she was a זונה.

steps.title: She always covered her face at home
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that תמר covered her face in יהודה's house, so he did not recognize her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: It means that she covered her face in her father-in-law's house.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the question. 'She covered her face' describes how she always acted at home, not what she did on the road.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because תמר was always modest in יהודה's house, he had never seen her face. So when he met her on the road he did not recognize her, and he took her for a זונה. The covering explains why he didn't know her, not why he thought she was a זונה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
That she covered her face in her father-in-law's house.
phrases.notes: Her father-in-law is יהודה himself, so he never saw her face.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: שֶׁכִּסְּתָה פָּנֶיהָ בְּבֵית חָמִיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the פסוק: the covering refers to her past behavior at home.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The covered face was the sign that made יהודה think she was a זונה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Her habit of covering her face at home is why יהודה didn't recognize her.

steps.title: A modest daughter-in-law merits kings and prophets
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן teaches that a daughter-in-law who is modest in her father-in-law's house will have kings and prophets among her descendants.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: Any daughter-in-law who is modest in her father-in-law's house merits that kings and prophets come from her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related teaching that connects to רבי אלעזר's answer. It shows how great תמר's modesty was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר said תמר was modest in her father-in-law's house. This teaching adds that such modesty brings a reward: kings and prophets among her children. The proof is coming in the next steps.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said
that Rabbi Yonatan said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל כַּלָּה שֶׁהִיא צְנוּעָה בְּבֵית חָמִיהָ —
phrases.english: Any daughter-in-law who is modest in her father-in-law's house
merits that kings and prophets come out from her.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports and expands רבי אלעזר's picture of תמר's modesty.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Modesty in a father-in-law's house earns descendants who are kings and prophets.

steps.title: Where do we learn this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי יונתן's teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: This question sets up the proof that follows. The גמרא wants to know how we know that modesty brings this reward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A claim this specific needs a source. The answer will point to תמר herself.

phrases.english: From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the teaching in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for רבי יונתן's teaching.

steps.title: From תמר: ישעיהו and דוד
steps.stepSummary: The proof is תמר: prophets came from her, like ישעיהו, and kings came from her, like דוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: From תמר. Prophets, as it says: 'The vision of ישעיהו son of אמוץ.' Kings, from דוד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that תמר is the example. It shows both kings and prophets among her descendants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד comes from תמר through פרץ, so the kings are clear. The prophet example, ישעיהו, needs a link to her family. Quoting his father's name, אמוץ, sets up that link, which the next step explains.

keyTerms.meaning: The prophet ישעיהו, son of אמוץ

phrases.english: From Tamar.
Prophets, as it is written:
'The vision of Isaiah son of Amoz.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 1:1

phrases.english: Kings, from David.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers מנלן from step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: תמר, whose descendants include the prophet ישעיהו and King דוד.

steps.title: ישעיהו's father was a king's brother
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי gives a tradition that אמוץ and King אמציה were brothers, so ישעיהו is from דוד's family.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי said: This is a tradition we received from our ancestors: אמוץ and אמציה were brothers.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי לוי supplies the missing link. It shows why ישעיהו counts as a descendant of תמר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אמציה was a king of the line of דוד. If ישעיהו's father אמוץ was his brother, then ישעיהו is also from דוד's family, and so from תמר. This completes the proof that prophets came from her.

keyTerms.meaning: A king of יהודה from דוד's line

steps.whatToRemember: תמר's modesty earned her both kings (דוד) and prophets (ישעיהו, whose father was the brother of King אמציה).

phrases.english: And Rabbi Levi said:
This matter is a tradition in our hands from our ancestors:
Amoz and Amaziah were brothers.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי: דָּבָר זֶה מָסוֹרֶת בְּיָדֵינוּ מֵאֲבוֹתֵינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the family link needed for the ישעיהו proof in step 8.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A received tradition that אמוץ and King אמציה were brothers.

steps.title: Why the odd word מוצאת?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says היא מוצאת, but the expected word for 'being brought out' is מיתוצאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'she was brought out' (מוצאת). It should have said מיתוצאת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to another פסוק in the story and points out an unusual word. It expects a different form of the verb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מיתוצאת would simply mean 'she was being taken out' to judgment. מוצאת can also hint at 'found.' The unusual choice suggests a hidden message, which the next step explains.

phrases.english: 'She was brought out.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 38:25

phrases.english: It should have said 'she was being brought out'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to a new פסוק in the יהודה and תמר story.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The normal form would be מיתוצאת, so the choice of מוצאת needs explaining.

steps.title: The angels moved her proof-items
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that סמאל hid תמר's signs and גבריאל brought them back, so they were 'found.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: After her signs were found, סמאל came and moved them far away, and גבריאל came and brought them close again.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר explains the odd word. מוצאת hints that her signs were 'found' again after being taken away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her signs were the items יהודה had given her, which proved he was the father. סמאל tried to keep them from her. גבריאל returned them, so she could prove her case and be saved. The word מוצאת, with its hint of 'found,' points to this.

keyTerms.meaning: Her signs: the items proving יהודה was the father
Moved them far away / brought them close

steps.whatToRemember: The word מוצאת hints that תמר's proof was 'found' again: סמאל took it away, and גבריאל brought it back.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
After her signs were found,
phrases.notes: Her signs are the items יהודה left with her (בראשית 38:18).

phrases.english: Samael came and moved them far away,
Gabriel came and brought them close.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: לְאַחַר שֶׁנִּמְצְאוּ סִימָנֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the unusual word as a hint to a hidden event.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מוצאת is just an odd way of saying 'she was brought out.'
steps.terutzMaskana: מוצאת hints that her signs were lost and then found again with גבריאל's help.

steps.title: A Psalm hints at תמר becoming like a silent dove
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא links the story of תמר's hidden signs to a פסוק in תהלים, and רבי יוחנן explains that when her signs were taken away, she became like a mute dove.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the פסוק means: 'For the leader, upon the mute dove of the distant ones, a מכתם of David.' רבי יוחנן says: from the moment her signs were taken away, she became like a mute dove.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק from תהלים that fits the story from the last step. רבי יוחנן reads it as describing תמר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11 we learned that סמאל hid תמר's signs. Now רבי יוחנן reads 'יונת אלם רחוקים' as 'a mute dove whose signs were made distant.' Without her signs, תמר had no way to speak up and prove her case.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what is written; a פסוק that fits what was just said
Distant; read here as her signs being taken far away
Her signs, meaning the items יהודה left with her

phrases.english: This is what is written:
"For the leader, upon the mute dove of the distant ones,
phrases.notes: תהלים 56:1

phrases.english: a מכתם of David."
Rabbi Yochanan says:
From the moment that her signs were taken far away,
she became like a mute dove.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אלעזר's story of the hidden signs with a פסוק
steps.raayaObject: That תמר's signs were hidden, leaving her helpless

steps.title: First meaning of מכתם: דוד was humble and wholesome
steps.stepSummary: The words 'לדוד מכתם' show that דוד came from תמר, and that he was מך (humble) and תם (wholesome) toward everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A מכתם of David' means that דוד came out of her, and he was humble and wholesome with everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the end of the same פסוק. It splits the word מכתם into two smaller words describing דוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק joins the silent dove (תמר) with דוד, showing that דוד descends from her. The word מכתם is read as מך + תם: humble and complete in character.

keyTerms.meaning: A word in the heading of some תהלים, explained here in several ways

phrases.english: "A מכתם of David":
that David came out from her,
for he was humble and wholesome with everyone.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is splitting מכתם into two words: מך (humble) and תם (whole).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the same פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מכתם = מך ותם; דוד, who came from תמר, was humble and wholesome with all

steps.title: Second meaning of מכתם: דוד was born circumcised
steps.stepSummary: Another reading: מכתם means 'his wound was complete,' meaning דוד was born already circumcised.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: מכתם means his 'wound' was already whole, because he was born circumcised.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second way to read the word מכתם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here מכתם is read as מכה + תמה, 'the wound is complete.' The place that would normally need the cut of מילה was already finished at birth.

phrases.english: Another explanation: "מכתם" —
that his "wound" was complete,
phrases.notes: The "wound" is the spot where מילה is done; for דוד it was already finished.

phrases.english: meaning that he was born already circumcised.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second reading of the same word
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מכתם = מכה תמה; דוד was born circumcised

steps.title: Third meaning of מכתם: דוד stayed humble even as king
steps.stepSummary: A third reading: just as דוד humbled himself to learn תורה when he was young, he stayed just as humble when he became great.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation of מכתם: just as in his youth he made himself small before anyone greater than him in order to learn תורה, so too he did when he became great.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third meaning of מכתם, focused on דוד's lifelong humility.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This goes back to the idea of מך and תם, but adds time: his humility was complete through his whole life. Becoming king did not change how he treated his teachers.

keyTerms.meaning: In his youth, when he was small
He made himself small, humbled himself
In his greatness, when he became king

steps.whatToRemember: The three meanings of מכתם: humble and wholesome with all, born circumcised, and humble his whole life, even as king.

phrases.english: Another explanation: "מכתם" —
just as in his youth

phrases.aramaic: הִקְטִין עַצְמוֹ אֵצֶל מִי שֶׁגָּדוֹל מִמֶּנּוּ
phrases.english: he made himself small before someone greater than him
in order to learn Torah,
so too in his greatness.
phrases.notes: Even after he became king, he still humbled himself the same way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third reading of the same word
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד's humility was complete (מך + תם) from youth through kingship

steps.title: Why did תמר only hint instead of naming יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says תמר sent a message: 'By the man who owns these I am pregnant.' The גמרא asks why she didn't just tell him plainly that it was him.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'She sent to her father-in-law, saying: By the man to whom these belong I am pregnant.' But she should have just told him outright!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the story of תמר and challenges the wording: why such an indirect message?
steps.deeperAnalysis: תמר was about to be burned, and naming יהודה could have saved her. So it is strange that she only hinted. The גמרא wants to know why she risked her life this way.

keyTerms.meaning: Let her just say it to him directly!

phrases.english: "And she sent to her father-in-law, saying:
phrases.notes: בראשית 38:25

phrases.aramaic: לְאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר אֵלֶּה לּוֹ אָנֹכִי הָרָה״.
phrases.english: By the man to whom these belong I am pregnant."
But let her just say it to him outright!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the תמר story after the side discussion about מכתם
steps.kashyaTarget: The indirect wording of תמר's message
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Her life was in danger, so she should have named יהודה plainly instead of hinting

steps.title: Better to be thrown into a fire than to shame someone in public
steps.stepSummary: Several chains of sages teach: it is better for a person to throw himself into a fiery furnace than to embarrass another person in public. That is why תמר only hinted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זוטרא בר טוביה says in the name of רב (some say רב חנא בר ביזנא in the name of רבי שמעון חסידא, and some say רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי): It is better for a person to throw himself into a fiery furnace than to shame his friend in public.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: תמר hinted so she would not shame יהודה in public, even though it could have cost her life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer gives a broad rule of behavior: shaming someone publicly is so serious that one should prefer being burned. By hinting, תמר left it up to יהודה to admit it himself, and she was ready to die if he didn't.

keyTerms.meaning: Make his friend's face pale, meaning to shame him

steps.whyThisMatters: This is one of the best-known teachings about how serious it is to embarrass someone in public.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה אָמַר רַב,
phrases.english: Rav Zutra bar Toviyah says that Rav says,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַב חָנָא בַּר בִּיזְנָא
phrases.english: and some say Rav Chana bar Bizna says
that Rabbi Shimon Chasida says,
and some say Rabbi Yochanan says
in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
It is better for a person
to throw himself into a fiery furnace,
and not make his friend's face pale in public.
phrases.notes: "Make pale" means to embarrass, because the blood drains from a shamed person's face.

steps.triggerLanguage: נוֹחַ לוֹ לָאָדָם שֶׁיַּפִּיל עַצְמוֹ לְתוֹךְ כִּבְשַׁן הָאֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers why תמר only hinted
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a moral principle that explains her behavior
steps.terutzHavaAmina: She should have saved herself by naming יהודה openly
steps.terutzMaskana: She hinted on purpose, choosing possible death over shaming יהודה in public

steps.title: The source for this rule is תמר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn this rule, and answers: from תמר.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this? From תמר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the loop: the rule just stated is learned from תמר's own behavior.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule was given to explain תמר, and now תמר becomes the proof of the rule. Her willingness to be burned rather than expose יהודה shows the principle in action.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

steps.whatToRemember: תמר chose to risk being burned rather than shame יהודה publicly; from her we learn not to embarrass anyone in public.

phrases.english: From where do we know this?
From Tamar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the rule in step 17
steps.raayaObject: The rule that one should prefer a fiery furnace over shaming someone in public

steps.title: יהודה was told with the same word he once used: הכר
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא teaches: יהודה gave his father bad news with the word הכר, and now he himself was given news with the word הכר.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Recognize, please.' רבי חמא ברבי חנינא says: with 'recognize' he gave news to his father, and with 'recognize' they gave news to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next words of תמר's message, הכר נא. רבי חמא ברבי חנינא points out a measure-for-measure link.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהודה once used the word הכר when showing יעקב the bloody coat of יוסף. Now that same word comes back to him through תמר.

phrases.english: "Recognize, please."
Rabbi Chama, son of Rabbi Chanina, says:
With "recognize" he brought news to his father —
phrases.notes: "He" is יהודה, and his father is יעקב.

phrases.english: with "recognize" they brought news to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: בְּהַכֶּר בִּישֵּׂר לְאָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next words of תמר's message
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Measure for measure: יהודה used הכר with יעקב, and הכר was used with him

steps.title: The two פסוקים that both use הכר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows the two places: 'הכר נא הכתנת בנך היא' (יהודה to יעקב) and 'הכר נא למי' (תמר to יהודה).
steps.simpleTranslation: With 'recognize' he informed: 'Recognize, please, is this your son's coat?' With 'recognize' they informed him: 'Recognize, please, whose these are.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the two פסוקים that prove רבי חמא's point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק is from the sale of יוסף, when the brothers showed יעקב the coat. The second is תמר's message to יהודה. The same phrase הכר נא appears in both, showing the measure-for-measure link.

phrases.english: With "recognize" he informed:
"Recognize, please: is this your son's coat?"
phrases.notes: בראשית 37:32

phrases.english: With "recognize" they informed him:
"Recognize, please, whose these are."
phrases.notes: בראשית 38:25

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּהַכֶּר בִּישֵּׂר: הַכֶּר נָא הַכְּתֹנֶת בִּנְךָ הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the פסוקים behind רבי חמא's teaching
steps.raayaObject: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא's measure-for-measure teaching

steps.title: נא means 'please': תמר begged יהודה not to look away
steps.stepSummary: The word נא always means a request. תמר was pleading with יהודה: please, think of your Creator and don't turn your eyes away from me.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Please.' The word נא is always a word of request. She said to him: I beg you, recognize the face of your Creator, and do not hide your eyes from me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the last word of the phrase, נא, and what תמר was really asking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since נא means 'please,' her message was not an accusation but a plea. She asked יהודה to think of his Creator and not ignore her, leaving it to him to admit the truth himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Hide or turn away your eyes, ignore

steps.whatToRemember: תמר's words הכר נא were a gentle plea, not a public accusation, which fits the rule of not shaming someone in public.

phrases.english: "Please."
The word "נא" is nothing but a word of request.
She said to him: I am asking you, please,
recognize the face of your Creator,
and do not hide your eyes from me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second word of הכר נא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נא means a request; תמר pleaded with יהודה to think of his Creator and not ignore her

steps.title: יוסף sanctified ה׳'s name in private and gained one letter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא links the פסוק 'ויכר יהודה' to רבי שמעון חסידא's teaching. יוסף sanctified ה׳'s name in private, so one letter of ה׳'s name was added to his name.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And יהודה recognized and said: She is more righteous than I.' This fits what רבי שמעון חסידא taught: יוסף sanctified Heaven's name in private, so he earned one letter of ה׳'s name added to his own, as the פסוק writes 'ביהוסף'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes יהודה's admission and brings a teaching that compares יוסף and יהודה. This step gives the יוסף half, which sets up the יהודה half in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'היינו' means 'this is what that sage meant.' יוסף's קידוש השם happened where no one saw it, so his reward is partial: one letter, the ה in 'יהוסף'. This prepares the contrast with יהודה, whose act was public.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what [so-and-so] said; it links a story to a known teaching
Sanctified Heaven's name; brought honor to ה׳

phrases.english: "And Yehudah recognized, and said: She is more righteous than I."
phrases.notes: בראשית 38:26

phrases.aramaic: הַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רַב חָנִין בַּר בִּיזְנָא
phrases.english: This is what Rav Chanin bar Bizna said
that Rabbi Shimon Chasida said:
Yosef, who sanctified the name of Heaven in private,
merited that one letter was added to him
from the name of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
as it is written: "He placed it as a testimony in Yehosef."
phrases.notes: תהלים 81:6. The name is normally spelled יוסף; here it has an extra ה, a letter from ה׳'s name.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רַב חָנִין בַּר בִּיזְנָא אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן חֲסִידָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from תמר's plea to יהודה's response, his admission.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A private קידוש השם earned יוסף one letter of ה׳'s name.

steps.title: יהודה sanctified ה׳'s name in public and his whole name carries it
steps.stepSummary: יהודה sanctified ה׳'s name in public, so his entire name contains ה׳'s name.
steps.simpleTranslation: יהודה, who sanctified Heaven's name in public, earned that his whole name is called by ה׳'s name.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes the comparison. יהודה's public admission earns a bigger reward than יוסף's private act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is סתר (private) versus פרהסיא (public). A public קידוש השם is greater, so יהודה gets the whole name and not only one letter. The four letters of ה׳'s name all appear inside יהודה.
steps.whatToRemember: Private קידוש השם earns one letter (יוסף). Public קידוש השם earns the whole name (יהודה).

phrases.english: Yehudah, who sanctified the name of Heaven in public,
merited that all of it is called

phrases.aramaic: עַל שְׁמוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא.
phrases.english: by the name of the Holy One, Blessed be He.
phrases.notes: All four letters of ה׳'s name are inside the name יהודה, with an added ד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the comparison begun with יוסף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A public קידוש השם earned יהודה the complete name of ה׳ within his own name.

steps.title: A בת קול promises to save three of יהודה's descendants from fire
steps.stepSummary: Because יהודה's admission saved תמר and her two unborn sons from burning, a בת קול promised that three of his descendants would be saved from fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once he admitted and said 'She is more righteous than I,' a heavenly voice said: You saved תמר and her two sons from the fire. By your life, in your merit I will save three of your children from the fire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא describes a second reward for יהודה's admission, one that matches what he did measure for measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהודה's honesty saved three lives from fire: תמר and her twins. So ה׳ rewards him by saving three of his descendants from fire. The count and the danger match exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: By your life; a form of oath

phrases.english: Once he admitted and said: "She is more righteous than I,"
a heavenly voice came out and said:
You saved Tamar
and her two sons from the fire.
phrases.notes: Her twins were still unborn, so she was carrying them when she was sentenced to burning.

phrases.english: By your life, I will save in your merit
three of your children from the fire.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן שֶׁהוֹדָה וְאָמַר צָדְקָה מִמֶּנִּי יָצְתָה בַּת קוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another reward for the same admission.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saving three from fire earned the rescue of three descendants from fire.

steps.title: Who are the three descendants?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which three descendants were saved.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who are they?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to identify the three descendants. It sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The promise left the three people unnamed. This question is not a challenge. It only asks for the names.

phrases.english: Who are they?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the identity of the three mentioned in the promise.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the three descendants saved from fire.

steps.title: חנניה, מישאל and עזריה
steps.stepSummary: The three are חנניה, מישאל and עזריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: חנניה, מישאל and עזריה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the three are חנניה, מישאל and עזריה, who came out of the furnace alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These three came from שבט יהודה and were thrown into נבוכדנצר's furnace. Their rescue fulfills the promise made to יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: The three young men saved from the furnace

phrases.english: Chananyah, Mishael, and Azaryah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of who the three were.

steps.title: How did יהודה know the child was his?
steps.stepSummary: Reading 'ממני' as 'from me,' the גמרא asks how יהודה knew that תמר's pregnancy came from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'צדקה ממני': how did he know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads 'ממני' as 'from me,' meaning יהודה admitted he was the father. It then asks how he could be sure. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pledge items only proved that he had been with her. They did not prove that the pregnancy was from him. So the גמרא wants to know where his certainty came from.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'ממני' is read as 'from me' (I am the father), not only 'more than me.' That second reading is what makes the question work.

phrases.english: "She is righteous; from me."
phrases.notes: The גמרא reads ממני here as "from me": the pregnancy is from יהודה.

phrases.english: How did he know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the words of the פסוק and asks a new question about them.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source of יהודה's certainty that he was the father.

steps.title: A heavenly voice said: these hidden things came from Me
steps.stepSummary: A בת קול announced that these hidden events came from ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: A heavenly voice came out and said: From Me came these hidden matters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a בת קול spoke the word 'ממני' and revealed that the whole event was ה׳'s hidden plan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ממני' is now split. 'צדקה' is יהודה's statement, and 'ממני' is ה׳ saying 'from Me.' Heaven confirmed that this was part of a hidden plan, so יהודה could be sure.

phrases.english: A heavenly voice came out and said:
From Me these hidden matters came out.
phrases.notes: ה׳ is the one saying "from Me": this was His hidden plan all along.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָצְתָה בַּת קוֹל וְאָמְרָה מִמֶּנִּי יָצְאוּ כְּבוּשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers how יהודה knew.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A בת קול revealed it by saying 'ממני', meaning the events came from ה׳.

steps.title: Once he knew her, יהודה never separated from her
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר אמי reads 'ולא יסף' to mean that יהודה never stopped living with תמר.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he did not continue to know her again.' שמואל סבא, father-in-law of רב שמואל בר אמי, said in his name: once he knew her, he never again stopped from her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a surprising reading of the end of the פסוק. It does not mean he left her. It means he never stopped being with her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, 'ולא יסף' sounds like 'he did not do it again.' רב שמואל בר אמי flips this to 'he did not stop.' The proof for this reading comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And he did not add / did not stop (two possible meanings)

steps.confusionAlert: The plain meaning seems to be 'he never did it again.' The גמרא reads the exact opposite: 'he never stopped.'

phrases.english: "And he did not continue to know her again."
phrases.notes: בראשית 38:26. "Know" here means living with her as husband and wife.

phrases.english: Shmuel the Elder said,
the father-in-law of Rav Shmuel bar Ami,
in the name of Rav Shmuel bar Ami:
once he knew her,
he never again stopped from her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל סָבָא חֲמוּהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to explain the next words of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'ולא יסף' means יהודה never stopped living with תמר.

steps.title: Proof from the great voice at Sinai that did not stop
steps.stepSummary: A גזירה שוה with 'קול גדול ולא יסף' from מתן תורה shows that 'יסף' can mean 'did not stop.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written here: 'ולא יסף עוד לדעתה,' and it is written there: 'a great voice that did not stop.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the previous reading by pointing to the same word at מתן תורה. There, 'ולא יסף' means the voice never stopped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At הר סיני, 'ולא יסף' describes a voice that kept going. Since the same word appears in both פסוקים, it carries the same meaning here: יהודה never stopped.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written here... and it is written there; the formula of a word comparison

steps.whatToRemember: The same word 'ולא יסף' at הר סיני means 'never stopped.' So יהודה never left תמר.

phrases.english: It is written here: "And he did not continue to know her again,"
and it is written there: "A great voice, and it did not stop."
phrases.notes: דברים 5:19, describing ה׳'s voice at הר סיני.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתִיב הָכָא וְלֹא יָסַף עוֹד לְדַעְתָּה וּכְתִיב הָתָם קוֹל גָּדוֹל וְלֹא יָסָף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the textual proof for רב שמואל בר אמי's reading.
steps.raayaObject: The reading that 'ולא יסף' means 'did not stop.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 5:19, 'קול גדול ולא יסף,' through a גזירה שוה.

steps.title: אבשלום sinned through his hair
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about אבשלום and brings a ברייתא that says he rebelled through his hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said אבשלום was proud of his hair. A ברייתא teaches: אבשלום rebelled because of his hair.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next example in the משנה, אבשלום, and brings a ברייתא saying his hair was the root of his sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the משנה's pattern of מדה כנגד מדה: the very thing a person sinned with is how he gets punished. Here the ברייתא names the sin: his pride in his hair led to his rebellion.

keyTerms.meaning: דוד's son, who rebelled against him

phrases.english: Avshalom was proud of his hair, etc.
The Rabbis taught:
Avshalom rebelled through his hair,

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבְשָׁלוֹם נִתְגָּאָה בִּשְׂעָרוֹ וְכוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of יהודה and תמר to the next case in the משנה, אבשלום.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבשלום's sin of rebellion came through his hair.

steps.title: The פסוק about אבשלום's beautiful, heavy hair
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings פסוקים describing אבשלום's beauty and his very heavy hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'There was no man as handsome as אבשלום... and when he cut his hair, which he did every year because it was heavy on him, he weighed his hair at two hundred שקלים by the king's stone.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא proves that אבשלום's hair was something special that he took pride in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק goes out of its way to praise his looks and to weigh his hair. That shows how central his hair was to him, which sets up the punishment that comes next.

phrases.english: As it is said:
"And there was no man as handsome as Avshalom, etc.
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 14:25–26

phrases.english: And when he shaved his head,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיָה מִקֵּץ יָמִים לַיָּמִים אֲשֶׁר יְגַלֵּחַ
phrases.english: and it was at the end of every year that he would shave it,
because it was heavy on him, so he shaved it,
and he weighed the hair of his head
at two hundred shekels by the king's stone."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the פסוק behind the ברייתא's claim.
steps.raayaObject: That אבשלום's hair was a source of pride for him.

steps.title: What the 'king's stone' was
steps.stepSummary: A תנא explains that the 'king's stone' was the stone used as a weight by the people of טבריא and ציפורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: it is a stone that the people of טבריא and ציפורי use to weigh with.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains an unclear word in the פסוק: what is the 'king's stone'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a side explanation of a word, not a new idea in the argument. It identifies the stone as a weight that was known and used in those cities.

phrases.english: It was taught:
A stone that the people of Teveria
and the people of Tzippori weigh with.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the phrase 'אבן המלך' from the פסוק just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'king's stone' was the weight used in טבריא and ציפורי.

steps.title: So he was hung by his hair
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: because he sinned with his hair, he was hung by his hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore he was hung by his hair.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא states the punishment that matched the sin. A פסוק as proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'therefore' ties the punishment directly to the sin. This is the מדה כנגד מדה the משנה is teaching.

phrases.english: Therefore he was hung by his hair,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the punishment that matches the sin from step 31.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבשלום's punishment came through his hair, just like his sin.

steps.title: The פסוק of אבשלום caught in the tree
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק describes אבשלום's head getting caught in a great tree while his mule rode on.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'אבשלום ran into דוד's servants. He was riding a mule, and the mule went under the thick branches of a great tree. His head got caught in the tree, and he was left hanging between heaven and earth, while the mule under him went on.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא proves from the פסוק that אבשלום ended up hanging by his head, meaning his hair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says his 'head' got caught, and the ברייתא reads that as his hair getting tangled. So the thing he was proud of became his trap.

phrases.english: As it is said: "And Avshalom happened upon David's servants,
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 18:9. Here וַיִּקְרָא means 'happened to meet', not 'called'.

phrases.english: and Avshalom was riding on the mule,

phrases.aramaic: וַיָּבֹא הַפֶּרֶד תַּחַת שׂוֹבֶךְ הָאֵלָה הַגְּדוֹלָה
phrases.english: and the mule went under the thick branches of the great tree,
and his head got caught in the tree,
and he was left between heaven and earth,
and the mule that was under him went on."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the claim of step 34.
steps.raayaObject: That אבשלום was hung by his hair.

steps.title: אבשלום tried to cut his hair
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that אבשלום took a sword and wanted to cut his hair to free himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: He took a sword and wanted to cut it off.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: אבשלום tried to save himself by cutting off the hair that held him. The next step tells why it didn't work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets up the next line. It shows he had a way out, so the next step must explain why he didn't use it.

phrases.english: He took a sword;
he wanted to cut it.
phrases.notes: 'It' means his hair, which was holding him to the tree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a story detail to the hanging in the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבשלום tried to cut himself free with a sword.

steps.title: The underworld opened beneath him
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught that right then, שאול opened up under אבשלום.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: at that moment, שאול split open beneath him.
steps.whatsHappening: This explains why אבשלום did not cut himself free: the underworld opened right under him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting his hair would have dropped him into the opening below, so he stayed hanging. That is how he remained stuck until he was killed.

keyTerms.meaning: the school of רבי ישמעאל taught

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
At that moment, the underworld split open beneath him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the attempt in step 36 failed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שאול opened beneath אבשלום, so he did not cut himself loose.
steps.whatToRemember: אבשלום sinned with his hair and was trapped by his hair: a clear case of מדה כנגד מדה.

steps.title: דוד cries 'my son' over אבשלום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes two פסוקים where דוד mourns אבשלום, saying 'my son' eight times in total.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The king was shaken, went up to the room over the gate and cried, saying: My son אבשלום, my son, my son אבשלום! If only I had died instead of you, אבשלום my son, my son.' And: 'The king covered his face and cried out loudly: My son אבשלום, אבשלום my son, my son.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next question by quoting דוד's words of mourning. Count the 'my son's: there are eight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is learned yet. The גמרא is laying out the פסוקים so it can ask why 'my son' is repeated so many times.

phrases.english: "And the king was shaken, and went up to the room over the gate,
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 19:1 and 19:5

phrases.english: and wept, and this is what he said as he went:
My son Avshalom, my son, my son Avshalom!
If only I had died in your place,
Avshalom my son, my son."
"And the king covered his face,
and the king cried out in a loud voice:
My son Avshalom, Avshalom my son, my son."
phrases.notes: Count them up: 3 in the first line, 2 in the next, 3 here, which makes eight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from אבשלום's death to דוד's mourning for him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד said 'my son' eight times when he mourned אבשלום.

steps.title: Why eight times 'my son'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the eight mentions of 'my son' are for.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why are there these eight 'my son's?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why דוד repeated 'my son' eight times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes that each repeated word in a פסוק has a purpose. So eight 'my son's should match up with eight things.

phrases.english: These eight "my son"s, what are they for?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the repetition in the פסוקים just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the eight repetitions of 'בני' accomplished.

steps.title: Seven to raise him from גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: Seven of the 'my son's raised אבשלום up from the seven levels of גיהנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: With seven of them, דוד raised him up from the seven levels of גיהנם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that seven of the cries lifted אבשלום out of the seven levels of גיהנם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each cry of 'my son' worked to pull אבשלום up one level. This explains seven of the eight; the eighth is discussed next.

phrases.english: Seven, with which he raised him up
from the seven levels of Gehinnom;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 39 for seven of the eight.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Seven 'בני's raised אבשלום from seven levels of גיהנם.

steps.title: Two views on the eighth 'my son'
steps.stepSummary: Some say the eighth brought אבשלום's head close to his body; others say it brought him into עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one: some say it brought his head close to his body, and some say it brought him into עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two opinions about what the eighth 'my son' did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both views agree that seven cries took him out of the seven levels of גיהנם. They differ only about the eighth. One view says it brought his head close to his body. The other says it brought him into עולם הבא.

phrases.english: And the other one:

phrases.aramaic: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: דְּקָרֵיב רֵישֵׁיהּ לְגַבֵּי גוּפֵיהּ,
phrases.english: some say that he brought his head close to his body;
and some say that he brought him to the World to Come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer to step 39 for the eighth 'בני'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either it joined his head to his body, or it brought him to עולם הבא.
steps.whatToRemember: דוד's eight cries of 'my son' were not just grief: seven raised אבשלום out of גיהנם, and the eighth did even more for him.

steps.title: What did אבשלום 'take'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק about אבשלום setting up a monument and asks what the word 'took' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And אבשלום took and set up for himself in his lifetime.' What does 'took' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new פסוק about אבשלום and asks about the strange word 'took', which has no clear object.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says he 'took' but does not say what he took. That gap invites a דרשה, which comes in the next step.

phrases.english: "And Avshalom took and set up for himself in his lifetime."
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 18:18

phrases.english: What is "took"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to a new פסוק about אבשלום.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word 'לקח' refers to in the פסוק.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: he made a bad deal
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says 'took' means אבשלום made a bad deal for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: he took a bad deal for himself.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש explains that 'took' hints that אבשלום made a bad bargain for himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש links לקח, 'took', to מקח, 'a deal'. The deal was bad because it led to his downfall.

keyTerms.meaning: a bad deal, a bad purchase

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
That he took a bad deal for himself.
phrases.notes: Wordplay: לָקַח (took) and מִקָּח (a deal) come from the same root.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: שֶׁלָּקַח מִקָּח רַע לְעַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 42.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'לקח' means he made a bad 'מקח' for himself.

steps.title: The 'King's Valley' as ה׳'s deep plan
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בר פפא reads 'in the King's Valley' as 'in the deep plan of the King of the world'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The monument that is in the King's Valley.' רבי חנינא בר פפא said: in the deep plan of the King of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next words of the same פסוק, reading 'King's Valley' as a hint to ה׳'s deep plan. His statement continues after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא בר פפא links עמק (valley) to עמוקה (deep), and reads 'the King' as ה׳. So what happened to אבשלום was part of ה׳'s hidden plan.

phrases.english: "The monument that is in the King's Valley, etc."
Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּעֵצָה עֲמוּקָּה שֶׁל מַלְכּוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם,
phrases.english: In the deep plan of the King of the world,
phrases.notes: Wordplay: עֵמֶק (valley) sounds like עֲמוּקָּה (deep). His sentence keeps going after this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פָּפָּא: בְּעֵצָה עֲמוּקָּה שֶׁל מַלְכּוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the same פסוק, moving to its next words.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'עמק המלך' hints to the deep plan of ה׳, the King of the world.
